title: K-flat resolutions in closed monoidal Grothendieck categories
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] whose tensor product is additive in each variable. Call an object $F$ flat if both $F\otimes-$ and $-\otimes F$ are exact. Suppose there is a functor $B:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ with flat values and a natural epimorphism $B\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$. For every $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complex $L$ in $\mathcal A$, there exist a complex $Q$ and a quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to L$ such that $Q$ is K-flat for the direct-sum total tensor product of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. No boundedness condition is imposed on $L$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_quasiIso_isKFlatForTotalTensor {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [MonoidalPreadditive C] [SymmetricCategory C] [MonoidalClosed C] (B : C ⥤ C) (hB : ∀ X : C, ObjectProperty.flat (B.obj X)) (ε : B ⟶ 𝟭 C) [∀ X : C, Epi (ε.app X)] (L : CochainComplex C ℤ) : ∃ (Q : CochainComplex C ℤ) (q : Q ⟶ L), QuasiIso q ∧ Q.IsKFlatForTotalTensor
lean.note: States only the requested two-sided binary total-tensor K-flat resolution, using the recorded dependency predicate. The upstream exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat additionally asserts termwise flatness and uses the monoidal kFlat interface; it is a proof source, not a verbatim statement match.
